title: Unique Paths
description: Count paths from top-left to bottom-right in an m×n grid moving only right or down. Classic 2D DP: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] + dp[i][j-1], with the entire first row and first column equal to 1.

notes: First row and first column are all 1 — there is exactly one way to reach any cell on the top edge (all rights) or the left edge (all downs).
Recurrence dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] + dp[i][j-1] says: paths to (i,j) = paths through the cell above + paths through the cell to the left.
Space can drop to O(n) by reusing a single row left-to-right (newRow[j] += newRow[j-1]).

questions.q: What is the recurrence for Unique Paths?
Why is the entire first row filled with 1?
options: There is exactly one path along the top edge — all moves are rights

questions.q: Time complexity of the 2D DP solution?
How can you reduce space from O(m*n) to O(n)?
options: Reuse a single row of length n, updating left-to-right
questions.explain: Each cell depends only on the cell above (previous row, same column) and the cell to the left (current row). One row suffices.

exercises.prompt: Fill in the 2D DP — first row/col are 1, then the recurrence.

blanks.hint: single path along any top edge or left edge
paths from above plus paths from the left

L3.prompt: Write `uniquePaths(m, n)` returning the number of paths from top-left to bottom-right moving only right or down. Log `uniquePaths(3, 7)`.
hints: Initialize the whole grid to 1 — that pre-fills the first row and first column.
For every interior cell, dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] + dp[i][j-1].
